data.title: Hungary recovers $20 million cash in probe of Orban minister
data.description:
Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, some buried in forests or hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, in a bribery probe into Miklos Sesztak, a minister under former right-wing leader Viktor Orban.

Prime Minister Peter Magyar ousted nationalist Orban after 16 years in power in an April election, pledging to mend ties with the European Union, marred by years of conflict under Orban, and to launch a sweeping anti-corruption drive into allegations of graft.

Two former ministers from Orban's government and former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy are ​under arrest over graft accusations in separate investigations. They have denied wrongdoing.

Authorities have also detained Orban's brother in a people-smuggling case, which the former leader had dismissed as an act of political revenge.

The clampdown is part of an anti-graft drive the centre-right Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory", considered "very important" by 70% of respondents in a survey by the Median pollster released on news website HVG this week.

"During the searches, investigators found large amounts of cash buried in forests, hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in a secluded location," the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said late on Friday.

The cash — 5.07 billion forints ($15.33 million), €2.66 million ($2.93 million) and $1.26 million — took a dozen State Treasury workers eight hours to tot up using five banknote counters, said Finance Minister Andras Karman.

Sesztak, who was Orban's development minister between 2014 and 2018, has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Gabor Papp, did not respond to an emailed request for comment on the recovery office's statement.

Magyar said the recovered cash signalled the end of what he described as a "mafia" led by Orban's right-wing Fidesz party and his Christian Democrat allies during Orban's 16-year rule.

Gabor Torok, a political scientist, said images of the large piles of cash were so vivid that they likely spelled doom for Fidesz, whose public support halved to just 16% of voters by November from levels before the vote, a Median survey showed.

data.title: China, US discuss tariffs, farm trade at first trade council meeting
data.description:
China and the United States held their first trade council meeting under a bilateral economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Friday, China's commerce ministry said on Saturday.

The two sides held "candid, in-depth and constructive discussions" on implementing outcomes from previous trade consultations, including tariffs, a reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement involving $30 billion on each side, agricultural trade and other issues of note, the ministry said.

Both sides will continue to use the council to address trade concerns, expand cooperation and reduce outstanding issues, it added.

data.title: Rocket Lab Hits 100 Electron Launches, Fastest Commercial Rocket to Reach the Milestone
data.description:
LONG BEACH, Calif., Nov. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation , a global leader in launch services and space systems, today announced mission success for its 100th Electron launch, setting a new record for reaching 100 launches faster than any other commercially developed rocket.

“The Mountain God Rises” mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 6:30 p.m. on November 14, 2026, deploying the YAMATSUMI-II synthetic aperture radar (SAR) Earth-imaging satellite to a 575km low Earth orbit for the Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space, Inc. (iQPS). This mission marks Rocket Lab’s 11th Electron launch for iQPS with 100% mission success since 2023. iQPS has booked seven more dedicated Electron launches through 2030 to complete its satellite constellation.

Reaching 100 launches in under a decade is a major milestone for commercial spaceflight. What started as a vision to open up access to space with the world’s first carbon-composite rocket has grown into an unmatched launch cadence across the small-launch industry.

Rocket Lab founder and CEO, Sir Peter Beck, says: “Few rockets reach 100 launches in their total operational lifetime. Not only has Electron now reached 100 launches, but it reached the milestone faster than any other commercially developed rocket. That record pace comes down to the relentless dedication of the Rocket Lab team, and I want to congratulate everyone behind Electron. This is the team that pioneered 3D-printed rocket engines, built the world’s first carbon-composite orbital rocket, launched back-to-back from two hemispheres, and shattered responsive space records along the way, putting Electron in a league of its own. To our customers who have trusted us with their spacecraft, many of them across multiple launches, thank you. The next 100 Electrons are already booked so we’re only accelerating from here.”

Since its first launch in 2017, Electron has deployed hundreds of satellites for commercial constellation operators, national security agencies, and scientific institutions from launch pads in New Zealand and Virginia. Backed by vertically integrated manufacturing and a packed manifest extending well into the next decade, Electron continues to deliver access to orbit while laying the operational foundation for Rocket Lab’s next medium-lift rocket, Neutron.

About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Driven by its industry-leading small-lift rockets Electron and HASTE and its upcoming reusable Neutron medium-lift rocket, Rocket Lab delivers reliable and responsive launch for the world’s most important missions from constellation deployment to missile defense. Rocket Lab’s satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com.

data.title: ICICI Bank credit card alert: 6 important changes to be introduced starting from 25 November; check affected cards
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Are you an ICICI Bank credit card holder? If that is the case, then you should be prepared for several changes in how you use your credit card. These changes will be introduced over the next few weeks and will include revised charges and the withdrawal of complimentary benefits scheduled between 25 November and 15 December 2026.

Do note that the new changes will impact different credit card categories at India's second-largest private sector bank, including premium, retail, business, and corporate variants.

The objective of these changes is to improve efficiency and streamline the customer usage and service experience for day-to-day users. Furthermore, while some customers will pay more for card replacement and 'priority pass' services, others will lose complimentary insurance protection and similar movie-related benefits.

Keeping this in mind, here are six key changes that will be implemented over the next few weeks, along with effective dates, possible implications, and the cards that will be impacted.

The first two changes will take effect on 25 November, i.e., in about 10 days. This will be followed by two revisions on 11 December. Finally, the remaining four benefit withdrawals will come into force on 15 December.

The complete details of the upcoming changes are discussed below:

The changes that are going to be introduced from December 15, require particular focus from eligible customers holding premium and co-branded credit cards, as they involve the withdrawal of benefits that may have initially impacted their choice of the card.

ICICI Bank is going to discontinue complimentary air accident and related insurance coverage on Emeralde Private Metal, Times Black, Emeralde Private, Emeralde, Diamant, Sapphiro and Rubyx cards.

Furthermore, it is essential to note that the cancellation for any reason (CFAR) cover is also going to be withdrawn from Emeralde Private Metal, Times Black, Emeralde and Emeralde Private cards. Not only this, separately, Parakram and Parakaram Select cardholders are going to lose their complimentary personal and air accident insurance coverage.

The banking institution is also going to discontinue the complimentary INOX benefit on 9 specified card variants. This will include Coral, Rubyx, Expressions and MakeMyTrip cards.

Therefore, for all eligible customers who consistently use these perks, features, and associated benefits, the upcoming changes may affect the overall value they receive from their credit cards. The higher replacement expenses and new 'priority pass' fee also mean that routine card-related services and day-to-day usage may become more expensive, depending on the kind of card an individual opts for and the associated terms and conditions.

In summary, it can be concluded that credit card users should carefully review the revised terms, conditions, and applicable rules for their specific variants before the respective effective dates, and those who are dependent on complimentary insurance may also need to analyse and assess whether they may require separate coverage rather than assuming that the existing card-linked protection is going to continue, and that any changes are only going to impact the new and upcoming users.

To eliminate such discrepancies and doubts, it is prudent to go through the latest developments and terms and conditions from official sources so that credit card spending, monthly budget and personal finance planning can be done accordingly.

data.title: Metals in the Age of AI — Game-changer or hyperscale hype?: Andy Home
data.description:
By Andy Home

Artificial intelligence may operate in the cloud, but its metallic roots lie in the earth.

Data centers wouldn't exist without a wide spectrum of metals, from galvanised-steel housing and copper wiring to rare earth magnets driving the servers. AI data centers are even more metals-intensive than traditional facilities. They are physically bigger, contain more computing hardware and use more power.

Investors have leaned into AI's metallic backbone.

Copper rode the AI investment wave to all-time highs earlier this year before becoming collateral damage in the recent technology-stock rout.

Tin , which has leapt from the Bronze Age to the AI Age via circuit boards, has been similarly rocked by broader tech turbulence.

But is AI demand for metals really the promised game-changer, or is it hyperscaled hype?

As with any new technology, there's a bit of both in the mix.

METALS TO (ARTIFICIAL) MIND

Data centers consume 60 to 75 metric tons of metals per megawatt (MW), according to a white paper by the World Economic Forum (WEF).

To put that into context, standard data centers use 5 to 10 MW of power, while AI hyperscaler facilities exceed 100 MW, according to the International Energy Agency. Hyperscalers are building the fastest, propelled by US-China competition for AI dominance.

Just about every metal you can name, and a few you probably can't, is deployed in the labyrinth of servers, chips, storage, networks, electrical systems, cooling systems and backup-power facilities.

Aluminium, copper and steel are everywhere in the building. More exotic elements such as gold, silver, cobalt and rare earths are concentrated in the core computing hardware. And backup power is currently a battleground of competing technologies, with lithium, lead and nickel-zinc batteries all fighting for market share.

But in terms of market impact, the three metallic standouts are gallium, germanium and tin. Data center demand will account for 6.0%, 2.4% and 1.2%, respectively, of global annual usage in 2035, according to the WEF report.

Gallium and germanium are tiny markets, and both are used in minute quantities, but they have an exponential impact on semiconductor performance.

China, the dominant producer of both metals, has restricted exports, which is why everyone else is scrambling to find alternative sources of two metals that are literally powering the global AI race.

Tin is less exotic and also remains a small market by base-metal standards, with annual consumption of just over 400,000 tons.

But since the phase-out of lead, tin has become the dominant material for soldering circuit boards. The more complex the ​data center architecture, the more tin it needs to bind everything together.

Copper comes in a distant fourth in the demand-impact table, with data centers accounting for less than 0.9% of global usage in 2035.

Moreover, data centers are likely to start using less copper and other metal as structural designs improve and operating processes become more efficient. Wood Mackenzie expects both copper and aluminium usage to peak in the early 2030s before declining over the rest of the decade.

Who knows, AI itself may be the lead engineer in this technical evolution.

BEYOND THE SERVER ROOM

Copper bulls shouldn't be too disheartened, though. The WEF estimates for data center metals usage stop at the door of the building, excluding the metals needed to provide the power that keeps the whole thing humming away in the clouds.

"The biggest metals story lies outside the facility itself" in the form of transmission lines, substations and energy infrastructure, according to Shashank Sriram, senior research analyst at consultancy Wood Mackenzie, speaking to DataCentre Magazine.

Connecting data centers to the grid or building co-located power plants requires significant volumes of copper, aluminium and zinc for galvanising steel towers and poles.

If power connectivity is included in the equation, actual demand for both copper and aluminium is three or four times the projections based solely on the physical facilities, Wood Mackenzie estimates.

And if data centers draw power from renewable sources such as solar and wind, the demand impact is magnified because these are also highly metal-intensive technologies.

Wood Mackenzie projects power-capacity additions for data centers to rise from 15-20 gigawatts (GW) a year today to 30-33 GW in the early 2030s.

This is where the AI investment meme melds with the existing electrification-of-everything theme. From a market perspective, the two are self-reinforcing bull narratives that are tricky to separate into component drivers.

RAGE AGAINST THE MACHINES

Everything, of course, depends on how many AI data centers are actually built in the next few years, which is where some of the hype comes in.

There are many estimates, all expressed in eye-watering trillions of dollars of investment.

However, many of the new megawatts of announced AI ​computing capacity can more accurately be described as "bragawatts", according to a study by the Oxford Smith School and financial broker Marex Group (8UU.F).

While media and markets price in a rapid, ⁠exponential ramp-up in AI infrastructure, the study says the true outcome is likely to be "a roll-out that is delayed, lumpy, and constrained by physical realities."

The single biggest bottleneck is grid connectivity. A data center can be built in 18 to 24 months, but the ​average US waiting time for a grid connection was four years between 2018 and 2023, the study found.

Compounding the physical hurdles is the growing political backlash against AI.

The Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections on November 3 included gubernatorial wins in Texas and Georgia, where Democrats campaigned in part on a moratorium on new data centers. The incoming Democrats are planning to unleash a flood of new legislation targeting AI systems and data center development when they take control of the US Congress in January.

And it's not just the US where public opinion is turning against the machines.

Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft ​data center in Amsterdam last week, part of coordinated protests across 16 countries under the "Stop Dirty Data Centres" banner.

Politicians are coming under increasing pressure to rein in what many see as the reckless build-out of a technology with unmatched potential to change the world in both good and bad ways.

Anthropic's warning in its IPO prospectus that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" doesn't really help the industry's cause.

POLICY CONTROLS

Government policy is likely to be as important as grid connection times in setting the pace of AI data center construction.

There's an analogy with the electric vehicle (EV) narrative that so excited battery-metal markets a few years ago.

The road to a fossil-fuel-free future has turned out to be a bumpy one, in part due to changeable government subsidy schemes.

The most glaring example is in the US, where President Donald Trump has rolled back his predecessor Joe Biden's subsidies for battery vehicles.

The result has been a collapse in EV sales in the world's second-largest automotive market. Sales in the first 10 months of this year were down 21% from the same period of 2025, according to consultancy Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

The AI metals revolution could turn out to be just as much a stop-start affair.

But another lesson can also be drawn from the EV sector.

The global roll-out of battery-powered vehicles may not have lived up to its early hype, but it hasn't stopped. Despite plunging sales in the US, global sales were still up 5% year-on-year in January to October.

In other words, governments can restrain growth of a new technology but they can't stop broader adoption.

HERE COME THE ROBOTS

Moreover, building AI's digital infrastructure is only the first part of this latest metals story.

"If digital AI is the brain of the next economy, embodied AI is the beginning of its body," according to Frank Nikolic, research principal for base and precious metals at CRU.

That means "machines that can sense, decide and act in the physical world, widening the addressable market from information work to real-world labour."

The robots are coming, and they are also built with metal.

Early deployment remains selective, CRU noted, but for some industrial functions such as logistics, sorting and inspections, embodied AI has already moved out of the laboratory and is being piloted in real-world environments.

"For commodity markets, the crucial point is not the novelty of the technology itself, but the fact that AI is moving from experimentation toward large-scale deployment and that needs metals and materials," according to Nikolic.

If you're starting to worry we're entering the realm of science fiction, specifically the Terminator films with their eponymous liquid-metal, shape-shifting humanoids, you may have good cause. Researchers are already working on soft robots, which can both handle delicate items, such as eggs, and change shape.

Much of the work centers on room-temperature liquid metals, which make soft robots "extremely deformable with higher degrees of freedom while navigating inside narrow and constrained spaces," according to researchers at China's Shenzhen University, writing for ScienceDirect.

Designers at Carnegie Mellon University in Pennsylvania unveiled a "proof of concept" nano liquid-metal robot in 2023 and, with a nice nod to the Terminator franchise, made it melt through the bars of an enclosed cage.

The metal they used was gallium.

It looks like we have a clear metals winner in the Age of AI.

data.title: BOE likely to raise rates further in 2027, Pill tells FT
data.description:
The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates further in 2027, over and above an increase at the next meeting in December, to combat inflation, Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill told the Financial Times in an interview published on Saturday.

Britain's central bank raised interest rates to 4% from 3.75% in its November meeting, the first rise since August 2023. Pill told the FT that hike was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, but that “we have further to go.”

“My view would be we will see evidence that motivates further rises” Pill told the newspaper, referring to the need for rate hikes next year, given the risks of second-round effects from elevated energy costs. “We will do what is necessary to get inflation back to 2% through time.”

British inflation, driven by second-round effects on wages caused by the ​Iran war, is likely to ‌rise to around 5% in the middle of next year, according to the BoE, which is more than double the central bank's target.

Pill considered an end to the US-Israeli conflict with Iran and a fall in energy prices to be a “very low probability,” signalling that he is set to vote for another quarter-point increase next month, the FT said.

"My bias, for what it’s worth, is that I worry about the inflationary impact being magnified by second-round effects,” he told the newspaper, adding that he believed that the central bank should have acted sooner to combat inflation. “In my view, we waited too long.”

Markets currently price in 90 basis points of tightening by end 2027, implying rates could get close to 5% in 2027. Pill said these expectations were “not outrageous.”

Because of the delays in hiking borrowing costs, “the ability to be modest [in the scale of rate rises] has diminished," he told the FT.

Pill signalled that he would not seek a third term as the bank’s chief economist when his current term ends in September 2027, according to the report.

data.title: Fed Vice Chair Says AI’s Trillion-Dollar Infrastructure Push Is Adding To Inflation Pressures
data.description:
Key points:
  • Jefferson said expectations of long-term productivity gains from AI are already having a significant impact on economic activity.
  • He pointed to rising equity prices, partly fueled by enthusiasm around the technology, as one factor boosting household wealth and spending.
  • Jefferson highlighted that meanwhile, companies are pouring money into data centers and related infrastructure to support AI model training and inference, driving a sharp increase in business investment.

Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson has warned that the massive artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout is adding to inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy, even as the technology promises to deliver substantial productivity gains over time.

Speaking at the University of California, San Diego, on Friday, Jefferson said the surge in AI-related investment is boosting demand, driving up prices of certain goods and adding to broader price pressures.

However, he expects those inflationary effects to ease as supply catches up and productivity gains begin to materialize.

Jefferson Says AI Boom Is Driving Investment, Household Spending

Jefferson said expectations of long-term productivity gains from AI are already having a significant impact on economic activity.

He pointed to rising equity prices, partly fueled by enthusiasm around the technology, as one factor boosting household wealth and spending.

Jefferson highlighted that meanwhile, companies are pouring money into data centers and related infrastructure to support AI model training and inference, driving a sharp increase in business investment.

“Firms are building and equipping new data centers on a very large scale to support model training and inference, driving rapid growth in aggregate business investment,” Jefferson said.

He added that this spending is already “putting upward pressure on resource utilization and the general price level.”

Memory And Logic Chips Face Supply Constraints

The Fed Vice Chair believes that the inflationary impact is particularly visible in industries struggling to keep pace with surging AI-related demand.

Jefferson pointed to memory and logic chips as examples of sectors where investment demand has outstripped available supply, contributing to steep price increases.

The implications extend beyond the semiconductor industry. Higher costs for components used in technology products and services are feeding into prices across the broader consumer economy.

Jefferson noted that the boom in demand for new technologies has been driving “unusually strong cost increases for consumer goods and services that depend on the same inputs, like memory.”

The pressure comes at a time when inflation remains considerably above the Fed’s 2% target. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.6% on an annualized basis in September, while core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, stood at 3.1%.

Productivity Gains Could Eventually Ease Inflation, Says Jefferson

Despite the near-term price pressures, Jefferson expects AI adoption to eventually expand the economy's productive capacity and help moderate inflation.

As semiconductor manufacturers and other suppliers increase capacity to meet demand, supply constraints should ease. At the same time, wider AI adoption could help businesses produce more with fewer resources, lowering production costs.

“My baseline view is that adoption of new technology will ultimately lift the economy's productive capacity substantially but gradually,” Jefferson said, while cautioning that the timing and magnitude of those gains remain uncertain.

He also highlighted the potential consequences for monetary policy, arguing that if AI-driven productivity growth encourages businesses to invest more and households to spend more, it could push the economy's neutral interest rate higher.

For now, inflation remains his primary concern. Following the Fed's decision to hold interest rates steady at its October meeting, Jefferson said the latest economic data showed persistent price pressures.

“Accordingly, I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal for determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy,” he said.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, declined 0.63%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) fell 0.83%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) was down 0.37%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) fell 1.29% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) declined 1.32%.

data.title: Ramayana effect? Prime Focus Q2 results: Revenue rises to Rs.1,410.17 crore; PAT climbs to Rs.91.04 crore from Rs.5.8 crore
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Prime Focus Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of Rs.58.27 crore in Q2 FY27. That was more than 14 times the Rs.4.06 crore it earned a year earlier. Strong demand for visual effects helped drive the increase in revenue and profit. Prime Focus is the parent company of visual effects and animation studio DNEG, the visual mastermind behind Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana.

Consolidated revenue from operations rose 35.2% to Rs.1,410.17 crore in the September quarter. The company posted operating revenue of Rs.1,042.89 crore in the same quarter last year. Operating revenue rose by Rs.367.28 crore from the same quarter last year. Total income, including other income, increased from Rs.1,071.85 crore to Rs.1,446.59 crore.

Profit before tax (PAT) climbed to Rs.91.04 crore from Rs.5.8 crore a year earlier. The company also recorded an exceptional loss of Rs.2.11 crore during the September quarter. The latest results marked a turnaround from the preceding June quarter. Prime Focus had posted a consolidated net loss of Rs.45.78 crore in that quarter.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated operating revenue reached Rs.2,666.25 crore. That compares with Rs.2,019.71 crore in the same period a year earlier.

That was a Rs.646.54 crore year-on-year rise. First-half net profit fell from Rs.114.52 crore to Rs.12.49 crore, partly due to exceptional expenses. The June-quarter loss absorbed most of the September-quarter profit.

Prime Focus disclosed raids by the Income Tax Department from October 7 to 14. The raids covered certain company offices and the homes of some directors. The department also seized some electronic records during the operation.

The company said it had cooperated with tax officials and supplied the documents they needed. Prime Focus said it had received no order when it approved the results.

It also said that it had received no demand or show-cause notice related to the search. The company saw no need to adjust its financial results following the proceedings.

Prime Focus Studios is producing the two-part Ramayana adaptation with Yash's Monster Mind Creations. DNEG is among the visual effects partners on the project. The studio lists Ramayana among its released projects, alongside Sky Force and Fighter.

Other released projects include Motor City, Eden and William Tell. The list also includes Those About to Die and The Garfield Movie. It also features Brahmāstra: Part One - Shiva.

The studio lists eight projects in production. These include The Angry Birds Movie 3, CoComelon: The Movie and The Garfield Movie 2. Animal Friends and Black Palace are also in production. The remaining titles are Blood on Snow, Bollywoof and Above the Below.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $2.35B in two weeks as BlackRock’s losing streak hits 11 sessions
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks, as redemptions reached more than $1 billion each week.

According to Farside Investors data, spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.07 billion between Nov. 9 and Nov. 13, following $1.28 billion in outflows the previous week, the largest weekly redemptions since late June.

The funds recorded $185.4 million in net outflows on Friday, down from $284.1 million on Thursday and $299.8 million on Wednesday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $143.5 million of Friday’s withdrawals, while Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) shed $41.9 million.

Friday marked the seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals, with about $1.71 billion redeemed since Nov. 5. The sustained outflows coincided with broader market weakness as Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on the same day.

BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF extends losing streak to 11 sessions

IBIT’s $143.5 million in net outflows on Friday extended the fund’s withdrawal streak to 11 consecutive trading sessions since Oct. 30.

The latest losses brought IBIT’s total net outflows over the 11-session streak to about $2.35 billion, extending withdrawals after outflows crossed the $2 billion mark on Wednesday.

IBIT shed $908.4 million during the latest week, following approximately $1.21 billion in withdrawals the previous week. Its November outflows reached $2.12 billion, accounting for roughly 90% of the broader Bitcoin ETF market’s net withdrawals during the month.

data.title: Strive CEO Says Bitcoin Could ‘Go To A Penny’ And The Company Would Still Survive Because It Has No Debt
data.description:
Key points:
  • Matt Cole said on Thursday that because Strive has preferred equity only, they have “no liquidation point.”
  • Strive has two securities, including SATA and SATS, which pays 13% and 15% dividends, respectively.
  • Cole said Strive had planned for Bitcoin falling as much as 80%.

Strive Inc. (ASST) CEO Matt Cole said that Bitcoin (BTC) “could literally go to a penny,” and the treasury company would still survive because it carries no debt that could force it to sell.

Speaking with Anthony Pompliano on the Pomp Podcast on Thursday, Cole explained that Strive raises money only through preferred stock, so there is no price at which its Bitcoin would be seized. “Because we have preferred equity only, no debt. We have no liquidation point,” he said.

He compared that to borrowing against Bitcoin, where a sharp drop can wipe out traders. “We see this in the coin markets every time it’s dropped. How many billions of dollars gets liquidated?” Cole said.

Strive has two such securities, Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA), which pays a variable 13% that rises to 13.25% in December, and Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Stock (SATS), which pays 15%.

ASST stock was trading over 1% down in overnight trading, after closing down 4% on Friday. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around ASST remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Built To Ride Out Bear Markets

Cole said Strive planned for Bitcoin to fall as much as 80%. To do that, it keeps about 85% to 90% of its balance sheet in Bitcoin and 10% to 15% in cash, which can cover its obligations during a downturn. “We could ride out any historical bear market without even having to sell a single Bitcoin,” he said. He added that the approach might even be too cautious. “Even if we had to sell 2% or 5%, that’s probably a reasonable risk for a company. You’re not blowing up,” Cole said.

Cole has made a similar case before. In June, he said Strive could keep paying dividends through a bear market mimicking one like 2022-23 using cash reserves, without selling Bitcoin.

A Bet Against The Dollar

Cole described the company’s structure as a long-term wager against the U.S. currency. Strive sells perpetual preferred stock, which pays dividends with no end date. “They will never stop debasing the U.S. dollar, and so we are perpetually short the U.S. dollar because we are selling a perpetual preferred equity, which will pay dividend forever,” he said.

Cole said Bitcoin needs to rise faster than SATA’s and SATS’s dividend rates over time for the company’s common shareholders to benefit.

That cushion is already being tested. Strive held 43,153 BTC bought at an average cost of $87,821 per coin. With Bitcoin’s price trading near $67,018 at the time of writing, that’s about 24% below Strive’s average purchase price.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

data.title: Swiggy, Zepto, Eternal rivals on same board: What govt's new gig worker welfare panel means
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Swiggy, Zepto and Eternal may compete for customers in India's quick commerce and food delivery markets, but representatives of the three companies will now share a platform to discuss the welfare of gig and platform workers.

In a LinkedIn post, Madhav Kasturia, founder and CEO Zippee, highlighted the constitution of the National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers, saying the government has brought competing platforms together to deliberate on social security for delivery partners and other gig workers.

While the government notification has not provided any names for the members of the board, Kasturia mentioned that Swiggy, Zepto and Eternal are on it.

The 22-member board includes representatives from Swiggy, Zepto and Eternal, as well as Urban Company, Rapido and workers' organisations, Kasturia said.

The Ministry of Labour and Employment notified the constitution of the board on October 30 under the Code on Social Security. The statutory body will recommend and monitor welfare schemes for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers.

These schemes could cover health and maternity benefits, accident and disability insurance, life insurance and old-age protection, according to Kasturia's post.

The development also has financial implications for aggregator companies. Kasturia pointed to provisions under the Social Security Code that require aggregators to contribute 1-2% of their annual turnover, subject to a cap of 5% of payments made or payable to gig workers.

The applicable contribution rate and the date from which it will take effect are yet to be notified, he said.

Such contributions could add to the costs platforms need to account for in their delivery economics.

Kasturia also flagged a practical challenge -- gig workers may work with multiple platforms, move between cities or switch between full-time employment and gig work. Ensuring that their records, eligibility and insurance benefits remain accessible across these transitions will be important.

The government's notification assigns the board the task of recommending suitable welfare schemes, advising the Centre on matters related to the Code and monitoring social welfare schemes. It will also review record-keeping functions at the state level and expenditure from the relevant fund and account.

The board is required to meet at least three times a year.

Kasturia said the recommendations and their implementation would determine how easily delivery partners can access these benefits when they need them.

data.title: US spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed $185 million as outflow streak hits seven days
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $185 million in net outflows on November 13. That made it seven straight trading days of investors heading for the exits.

Ethereum ETFs, meanwhile, pulled in $2.36 million on the same day. It is not exactly a stampede in the other direction, but in a week like this, any green on the board stands out.

The more precise figure from flow trackers, including Farside Investors, puts the Bitcoin ETF outflow at $185.4 million. Nearly all of it came from the two biggest names in the business.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the retreat with a $143.5 million withdrawal. Fidelity's Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) came second with $41.9 million in outflows.

Add those two together and you get the full $185.4 million. Every other spot Bitcoin ETF reported zero net flows for the day.

Across the full seven-day losing streak, Bitcoin ETFs shed roughly $1.91 billion. November 13's $185.4 million was less than a tenth of that total, which says something about how heavy the earlier days in the run were.

Zoom out to the month and the number gets bigger. Cumulative outflows for November have exceeded $2 billion month-to-date.

All of this happened while Bitcoin itself traded in a range of $68,000 to $73,000.

On the Ethereum side, the inflow was reported at approximately $2.3 million to $2.36 million depending on the tracker.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in the US in January 2024, and since then they have attracted net inflows of about $54.8 billion to $55 billion.

That cumulative figure has held up despite repeated outflow streaks throughout 2026. The current seven-day drain of roughly $1.91 billion represents a small slice of the total capital these products have gathered, under 4% of lifetime net inflows.

The research findings describe the outflows as pointing to growing wariness among institutional investors, driven by volatility and uncertainty around Bitcoin's price in recent weeks.

The concentration in IBIT and FBTC is the detail worth watching. When the two largest products account for 100% of a day's outflows, it suggests the selling is coming from a specific class of holder rather than a broad-based exodus across every fund.

The research notes the modest Ethereum inflows may hint at a shift in investor sentiment toward other crypto assets. A $2.36 million inflow against a $185.4 million outflow is not a rotation so much as a footnote, and one day of data does not make a trend.
